# x a of two limbs, a of T, on the guarded limbs and scalar

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `scale_entry_step_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x a$:

$$z \approx x a.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scale(x, a, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `T`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | `bool` | the step of the loop the function calls, once per element; not `constexpr`; rounds (loop `scale_2_entry`; the limbs of each element and a guarded, rule R3 on the factors of a fused operation) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the functions are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/batch.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include; a view of `T` is taken where the table writes a view of `const T`. They take no marker: a function on arrays compiles only while the kernels of its loop are proved ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - x a\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x a\rvert + \eta$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $2^{-105} \approx 2.4652 \times 10^{-32}$ | $2^{-47} \approx 7.1054 \times 10^{-15}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1074} \approx 4.9407 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-149} \approx 1.4013 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1p-105`, `0x1p-1074` | `0x1p-47f`, `0x1p-149f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1.0000000000001p-105`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1.000002p-47f`, `0x1p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `scale_entry_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/MapSteps.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/MapSteps.v), against `scale_entry_step_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions scale_entry_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition scale_entry_step_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 a : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  let '(z0, z1) := scale_entry_step_2 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 a in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((x0 + x1) * a)) <= 2 * u prec ^ 2 * Rabs ((x0 + x1) * a) + 1 * eta emin.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `scale_entry_step_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** scale_step_2 on the guarded limbs of x and the guarded a (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/scale_entry_step_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/scale_entry_step_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`scale_step_2`](scale_step_2.md).

```
# The step of scale_2, z = x a for arrays x and a scalar a that the program supplies (rule R3, the
# factors of a fused operation: architecture.md): scale_step_2 on the limbs of x and on a guarded.
# scale_step_2 (mul_2_1) only multiplies them, which R3 alone does not guard; but a compiler that sees
# the elements of x to be 1 fuses a product a = y z of the program into the fms of mul_2_1's two_prod
# (Apple clang 21 under -ffp-contract=fast at -O2 with NDEBUG, measured: every round). After the
# guards each is a number of the format. Its claims are those of scale_step_2: the guard is the
# identity on numbers of the format. scale_step_2 stays the step of bv_scale_2, whose array is stored.

gx0      = guard(x0)
gx1      = guard(x1)
ga       = guard(a)
(z0, z1) = scale_step_2(gx0, gx1, ga)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#scale_entry_step_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 96 516 720 | 0 | 1 − ε, ε < 10⁻⁹ | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 96 421 788 | 0 | 0.9999998510 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 3 907 277 | 0 | 0.972718 (`fp:6:-8:-2`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
